plan.contextChunk: This figure shows cyclohexane in its chair form through three labeled panels, (a), (b), and (c). Panel (a) is a ball-and-stick model of the six-membered ring: six dark gray carbon spheres joined by pale rods trace a shape that rises at one end and dips at the other, each carbon carrying two off-white hydrogen spheres. Panel (b) redraws the same ring as a line structure with the near bonds bolded to signal depth, its carbons numbered 1 through 6 in magenta and its hydrogens lettered in magenta, green, blue, and black. Two drawn eyes at the right, marked "Observer", send magenta dashed sightlines to carbon 1 and to carbon 5. Panel (c) is the corresponding Newman projection: two circles, each with a front carbon dot and three bonds, are joined at the top and bottom by groups written "CH2", with the front atoms numbered 1 and 5 and the surrounding hydrogens numbered 2, 3, 4, and 6 in matching colors. Carrying the same numbering and hydrogen colors through all three panels lets the reader map any position on the model onto the corresponding position in the end-on view. Together the panels demonstrate that the chair shape holds its bond angles near the tetrahedral value while keeping every pair of neighboring C-H bonds staggered, leaving the ring free of strain.

elements: Panel (a): ball-and-stick chair cyclohexane — six dark-gray carbon spheres in the chair ring (alternating up/down puckering), pale-gray cylindrical C–C bond rods
Panel (a): twelve off-white hydrogen spheres, two per carbon (one axial pointing straight up/down, one equatorial splayed outward), joined by pale rods
Panel (b): chair line structure of cyclohexane drawn as the classic zig-zag chair outline, with the two near (front) C–C bonds drawn as heavy bold lines for depth
Panel (b): magenta ring-position numerals 1–6 placed beside their carbons
Panel (b): twelve hydrogen letter labels on short bond lines — colored magenta, green, blue, and black to match panel (c)
Panel (b): two drawn eye icons at the right with gray lash/lid shading, labeled 'Observer'
Panel (b): two magenta dashed sightlines running from the eyes to carbon 1 and to carbon 5
Panel (c): two Newman projection circles side by side
Panel (c): front-carbon dot at each circle center with three bonds radiating from it (front atom), labeled '1' (left) and '5' (right) in magenta
Panel (c): three back-atom bonds per circle drawn to the circle rim, staggered 60° from the front bonds
Panel (c): hydrogen letters around each circle colored magenta, green, blue, black, with magenta numerals 2, 3 (left circle) and 4, 6 (right circle)
Panel (c): two 'CH2' text connectors joining the two Newman circles at top and bottom (ring carbons 6 and 3 respectively)
Panel labels '(a)', '(b)', '(c)' in bold black

interactions.teaches: The same chair cyclohexane can be read as a 3D model, as a line drawing, or as an end-on Newman projection — the numbering and hydrogen colors are preserved so any position can be tracked across all three.
interactions.label: Representation

interactions.teaches: Rotating the ball-and-stick model reveals the puckered chair geometry — that the ring is not flat, that bond angles stay near 109.5°, and that axial and equatorial C–H bonds point in distinct directions.

Clicking carbon 1 or carbon 5 in the line drawing highlights that front carbon, its two hydrogens, and the CH2 connectors in the Newman projection, showing exactly how a ring position maps onto the end-on view along the C1–C2 / C5–C4 sightline.

demo_steps.title: The 3D chair
demo_steps.narration: Start with the ball-and-stick model: six carbons pucker into a chair, each carrying one axial and one equatorial hydrogen. Drag to rotate and confirm the ring is not planar.

demo_steps.title: Where the observer stands
demo_steps.narration: The same ring as a line structure, numbered 1–6. Two eyes sight down the ring at carbon 1 and carbon 5 — those two sightlines are what the Newman projections capture.

demo_steps.title: The end-on view
demo_steps.narration: Looking down C1 and C5, every front C–H bond sits exactly between two back bonds: all neighboring C–H bonds are staggered, so the chair carries no torsional strain. Click carbon 1 or 5 to trace a position back to the line drawing.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World scale: use a ring C–C bond length of 1.0 unit so the whole figure spans roughly ±3 units. Ideal chair carbon coordinates (radius 1.25, pucker ±0.25): C_k at (1.25·cos(60k°), (-1)^k·0.25, 1.25·sin(60k°)) for k=1..6 — C1, C3, C5 up; C2, C4, C6 down. Carbon spheres r=0.30 in dark gray #4a4a50; hydrogen spheres r=0.20 in off-white #e6e4d8; bond rods radius 0.07 in pale blue-gray #b9c6d6 with a light specular highlight. C–H length 0.6 units; axial H points straight along ±Y from each carbon, equatorial H points outward and slightly opposite-Y, making the H–C–H plane bisect the ring exterior. Panel (b): chair drawn front-on (no orbit), long axis horizontal, spanning about 4 units wide × 2 units tall; the two bonds nearest the viewer (C1–C2 and C2–C3 region, the lower-front edge) drawn at ~3× line weight in black; numerals 1–6 in magenta #e6007e placed inside the ring next to each vertex — 1 lower-right, 2 lower-center, 3 lower-left, 4 upper-left, 5 upper-center, 6 upper-right. Hydrogen label colors as in source: C1 carries a green #00a651 equatorial H (right) and a blue #0072bc axial H (below); C2 carries a magenta #e6007e H; C4 and C5 carry magenta H labels above; C3 and C6 carry black H labels. Observer eyes: two almond eye icons with gray #d9d9d9 lid shading at the far right, x≈+3.2, one at y≈+0.3 the other at y≈-0.5; magenta #e6007e dashed lines run leftward from each eye — upper eye to carbon 5, lower eye to carbon 1 — each ending in a small arrowhead. Panel (c): two circles of radius 0.9, centers at x=-1.6 and x=+1.6, y=0; front carbon is a filled dot at each center with three bonds of length 0.9 at screen angles 90°, 210°, 330° (left circle) and 90°, 210°, 330° (right circle); back bonds drawn to the rim at 30°, 150°, 270°, i.e. staggered 60°. Left circle: center numeral '1' magenta; top bond H magenta with numeral '2' magenta beside the upper-left green H; upper-left and lower-left H letters green #00a651 (numerals 2 and 3 magenta); bottom H blue #0072bc. Right circle: center numeral '5' magenta; top H magenta with magenta numeral '4'; right-side H letters black; bottom H blue. 'CH2' text in black sits midway between the circles at y≈+0.75 (labeled 6, magenta numeral above it) and y≈-0.75 (labeled 3), with short bond lines linking each CH2 to the rim of both circles. Panel tags '(a)', '(b)', '(c)' bold black at the upper-left of each panel.
interactionPlan.notes: Render panel (a) with MeshPhongMaterial spheres plus CylinderGeometry bonds under one key directional light and soft ambient to reproduce the glossy ball-and-stick look; only this panel responds to OrbitControls. Panels (b) and (c) are flat 2D: build them with THREE.Line / LineSegments (or Line2 for variable thickness — bolded front bonds need ~3× linewidth) on the z=0 plane with an orthographic-style locked camera, and draw all letters/numerals as canvas-texture sprites so colors (#e6007e magenta, #00a651 green, #0072bc blue, #000 black) stay crisp. Dashed sightlines via LineDashedMaterial with computeLineDistances(). Eye icons as small canvas-texture planes. Switching panels should cross-fade opacity over ~300 ms rather than hard-cut, and should swap the camera/controls mode (orbit enabled only for (a)). For selectCarbon, keep a shared 'selected ring position' state: raycast against invisible sphere hit-targets at the carbon vertices in panel (b) and at the Newman circle centers in panel (c); on selection, tint the chosen carbon and its two H labels with a highlight ring/glow and dim non-selected labels to ~35% opacity so the correspondence pops.

authoredContext:
Cyclohexane adopts a strain-free, three-dimensional shape that is called a chair conformation because of its similarity to a lounge chair, with a back, seat, and footrest (the figure). Chair cyclohexane has neither angle strain nor torsional strain—all C−C−C bond angles are near the 109° tetrahedral value, and all neighboring C−H bonds are staggered.

The strain-free chair conformation of cyclohexane. All C−C−C bond angles are 111.5°, close to the ideal 109° tetrahedral angle, and all neighboring C−H bonds are staggered.

The ball and stick model, chair conformation, and Newman projection of cyclohexane. The carbon atoms are numbered in chair conformation and Newman projection.

The easiest way to visualize chair cyclohexane is to build a molecular model if you have access to a model kit, or alternatively to explore with one of the many computer-based modeling programs you may have access to.

Representation

You can also click carbon 1 or 5 in panel (b), or a Newman circle in panel (c).

1. The 3D chair
Start with the ball-and-stick model: six carbons pucker into a chair, each carrying one axial and one equatorial hydrogen. Drag to rotate and confirm the ring is not planar.
⚠ Figure failed to load

discrepancies: Panel (b): the ring is drawn from vertices that read as a slightly-squashed regular hexagon rather than the classic chair zig-zag (two pairs of parallel bonds, distinct 'seat/headrest' vertices) seen in the source, so the chair conformation is much less obvious in the line structure than in the original.

Panel (a): the ball-and-stick model sits well left of the canvas centre with the '(a)' tag floating far above-left of the molecule, unlike the tightly framed source panel; C–H bond lengths are also somewhat short relative to the C–C rods.

The source presents all three panels side by side for direct comparison; the generated figure only ever shows one panel at a time (toggle exists, so not missing, but the cross-panel 'same molecule, three views' comparison the source makes at a glance is lost).
Minor colour/assignment drift in panel (b) hydrogen labels (e.g. which H at C3/C4/C6 is magenta vs green vs black) relative to the source's specific colour coding.
evaluation.notes: A faithful and conceptually correct three-panel reconstruction (3D chair, numbered line structure with observers/sightlines, paired Newman projections with correct front/back carbon and CH2 connectivity), backed by strong interactions (panel toggle, carbon highlighting, clickable atoms, guided demo); weaknesses are the hexagon-like rather than chair-like line drawing in panel (b) and off-centre framing/tag placement in panel (a).

feedback.rationale: The concept and panel decomposition are correct (concept 5, no failure modes), but execution details—chair-shaped vertex geometry in panel (b), centering/tag placement in panel (a), and H label colors—need concrete rendering fixes.

interactionPlan.notes: Render panel (a) with MeshPhongMaterial spheres plus CylinderGeometry bonds under one key directional light and soft ambient to reproduce the glossy ball-and-stick look; only this panel responds to OrbitControls. Panels (b) and (c) are flat 2D: build them with THREE.Line / LineSegments (or Line2 for variable thickness — bolded front bonds need ~3× linewidth) on the z=0 plane with an orthographic-style locked camera, and draw all letters/numerals as canvas-texture sprites so colors (#e6007e magenta, #00a651 green, #0072bc blue, #000 black) stay crisp. Dashed sightlines via LineDashedMaterial with computeLineDistances(). Eye icons as small canvas-texture planes. Switching panels should cross-fade opacity over ~300 ms rather than hard-cut, and should swap the camera/controls mode (orbit enabled only for (a)). For selectCarbon, keep a shared 'selected ring position' state: raycast against invisible sphere hit-targets at the carbon vertices in panel (b) and at the Newman circle centers in panel (c); on selection, tint the chosen carbon and its two H labels with a highlight ring/glow and dim non-selected labels to ~35% opacity so the correspondence pops.

plan.authoredPrompt: This figure shows cyclohexane in its chair form through three labeled panels, (a), (b), and (c). Panel (a) is a ball-and-stick model of the six-membered ring: six dark gray carbon spheres joined by pale rods trace a shape that rises at one end and dips at the other, each carbon carrying two off-white hydrogen spheres. Two drawn eyes at the right, marked "Observer", send magenta dashed sightlines to carbon 1 and to carbon 5. Panel (c) is the corresponding Newman projection: two circles, each with a front carbon dot and three bonds, are joined at the top and bottom by groups written "CH2", with the front atoms numbered 1 and 5 and the surrounding hydrogens numbered 2, 3, 4, and 6 in matching colors. interactions.teaches: Rotating the ball-and-stick model reveals the puckered chair geometry — that the ring is not flat, that bond angles stay near 109.5°, and that axial and equatorial C–H bonds point in distinct directions.
